f: Do women have to make up missed fasts due to menstruation or post-partum bleeding?
b: Yes.

f: Does the blood of istiḥāḍah (chronic irregular bleeding) prevent prayer, fasting, or intercourse?
b: No.

f: What is the prescribed response to someone who intentionally neglects prayer or the Ramadan fast due to laziness?
b: They are to be punished severely (until blood is drawn) and imprisoned until they perform the act.

f: Under what conditions would one be executed for neglecting prayer or fasting?
b: Only if they deny the obligation of these acts or treat them with contempt.

f: Is it better to pray Witr in congregation during Ramadan or alone at the end of the night?
b: According to Qadi Khan, it is better in congregation during Ramadan, though others hold the contrary view.

f: Is a sick person required to leave a testament (Waṣiyyah) for missed prayers or fasts if they die while still unable to pray via gesture or before recovering?
b: No, they are not required to leave a testament for them.

f: In what cases must a sick person leave a testament (Waṣiyyah) for missed prayers and fasts?
b: When they missed them but were in a condition where they could have performed them (or made them up) but remained as a liability.

f: What is the required rate of payment for each missed prayer and fast (including Witr) when performing Isqāṭ (expiation)?
b: Half a Ṣā‘ of wheat (or its monetary value) per prayer or per day of fasting.

f: If a deceased person did not leave a testament (Waṣiyyah) for their missed prayers or fasts, can the guardian perform the Isqāṭ on their behalf?
b: Yes, a guardian may perform it voluntarily, and it is considered valid.

f: Can a living person perform the physical acts of prayer or fasting on behalf of the deceased?
b: No, one cannot physically pray or fast on behalf of the deceased.

f: How is fasting (al-Ṣawm) defined?
b: Refraining during the day from intentionally or mistakenly introducing anything into the stomach (or that which has the same ruling), and from sexual intercourse, with the intention (Niyyah).

f: Who is the fast obligatory for?
b: Those who are Muslim, sane, and pubescent.

f: Is knowledge of the obligation required for the fast to be mandatory?
b: Yes; for those who convert in hostile territory, it becomes mandatory once they learn of the obligation.

f: What are the conditions for the performance (Adā’) of the fast?
b: Physical health (no illness, menstruation, or post-partum bleeding) and residency (not traveling).

f: What are the conditions for the validity of the fast?
b: Intention, purity from menstruation/post-partum bleeding, and absence of things that invalidate the fast.

f: Is Janābah (major ritual impurity) a condition for the validity of the fast?
b: No, purity from Janābah is not a condition for validity.

f: What are the three types of fasts categorized as Farḍ?
b: Ramadan (both Adā’ and Qaḍā’), expiations (Kaffārāt), and vows (Nadhr).

f: What is the ruling for making up a voluntary fast that was spoiled?
b: It is Wājib.

f: What is the Sunnah way to fast ‘Ashura?
b: Fasting it with the 9th of Muharram.

f: Which days are considered Mandūb (recommended) for fasting?
b: Three days a month (especially the Ayyām al-Bīḍ—13th, 14th, 15th), Mondays and Thursdays, six days of Shawwāl, and any fast proven by Sunnah (like the fast of Prophet Dawud عليه السلام).

f: What is the ruling on fasting ‘Ashura alone without the 9th?
b: It is Makrūh Tanzīhī.

f: Which days are considered Makrūh Taḥrīmī to fast?
b: The two Eids and the days of Tashrīq.

f: What are some examples of disliked (Makrūh) fasts?
b: Isolating Friday or Saturday, fasting on the days of Nayruz or Mihrajan (unless by habit), Wiṣāl fasting (joining days and nights), and fasting an entire lifetime.

f: For which types of fasts is a specific intention not required?
b: Ramadan, time-bound vows, and Nafl (supererogatory) fasts.

f: What is the latest time one can form the intention for Ramadan, time-bound vows, or Nafl fasts?
b: Before mid-day (al-ḍuḥā al-kubrā).

f: What is the rule if a healthy resident intends a different type of obligatory fast during the month of Ramadan?
b: It still counts as a fast of Ramadan.

f: For which types of fasts is it required to make the intention from the night (Tabyīt)?
b: Qaḍā’ of Ramadan, Qaḍā’ of spoiled Nafl fasts, all Kaffārāt (expiations), and unconditional vows.

f: How is the beginning of the month of Ramadan established?
b: By sighting the crescent or, if the sky is overcast, by completing 30 days of Sha’bān.

f: Is it permitted to fast the Day of Doubt?
b: It is disliked, unless it is a Nafl (supererogatory) fast one is already in the habit of performing without wavering.

f: If the sky is overcast, what is the requirement for establishing the start of Ramadan?
b: The testimony of one just witness (including a woman, slave, or one previously punished for slander).

f: If the sky is clear, what is the requirement for establishing the start of Ramadan or Shawwāl?
b: A large congregation of people, the size of which is left to the discretion of the Imam.

f: Does eating, drinking, or having intercourse due to forgetfulness invalidate the fast?
b: No.

f: If you see someone who is fasting eating by mistake, should you remind them?
b: Yes, if the person is strong enough to fast; if they are not, it is better not to.

f: Does an emission of fluid caused by looking or thinking invalidate the fast?
b: No, even if it is persistent.

f: Does applying oil or kohl invalidate the fast, even if the taste is felt in the throat?
b: No.

f: Does Ḥijāmah (cupping) invalidate the fast?
b: No.

f: Does backbiting (Ghaybah) invalidate the fast?
b: No.

f: If a person intends to break their fast but does not actually do so, is the fast invalidated?
b: No.

f: Does tasting medicine invalidate the fast, provided one is mindful?
b: No.

f: If one wakes up in a state of Janābah (major impurity), is the fast valid if they remain that way throughout the day?
b: Yes, the fast is still valid.

f: Does pouring water or oil into the urethra invalidate the fast?
b: No.

f: Does water entering the ear (e.g., while swimming) invalidate the fast?
b: No.

f: Does scratching the ear with a stick repeatedly until earwax exits invalidate the fast?
b: No.

f: Does involuntary vomiting invalidate the fast?
b: No, even if it fills the mouth.

f: Does intentional vomiting of less than a mouthful invalidate the fast?
b: No (per the soundest view).

f: Does swallowing a food particle stuck between the teeth invalidate the fast?
b: No, provided the particle is smaller than a chickpea.

f: Does chewing something taken from outside the mouth invalidate the fast?
b: No, if it is the size of a sesame seed and is chewed until it disappears and no taste is felt in the throat.

f: Does intercourse invalidate the fast?
b: Yes, it requires both Qaḍā’ and Kaffārah for both the doer and the recipient (in either passage).

f: Does eating or drinking medication or sustenance invalidate the fast?
b: Yes, it requires Qaḍā’ and Kaffārah.

f: If someone mistakenly believes an act breaks the fast (e.g., applying oil to the mustache) and then eats, does Kaffārah apply?
b: If they act based on a jurist's ruling or a Hadith they do not fully understand, Kaffārah is not required. If they know the correct interpretation, Kaffārah applies.

f: What is the ruling for acts that break the fast but do not require Kaffārah?
b: Only Qaḍā’ (making up the day) is required.

f: Does using an enema (Iḥtiqān) invalidate the fast with Kaffārah?
b: No, it only requires Qaḍā’.

f: Does rainwater or snow entering the throat invalidate the fast if not swallowed intentionally?
b: According to the soundest view, it requires Qaḍā’ (but no Kaffārah).

f: If a person remembers they are fasting while eating, but then continues to eat intentionally, what is the ruling?
b: According to the soundest view, it requires Qaḍā’.

f: What is the ruling if one breaks their fast thinking the sun has set, only to realize it is still visible?
b: It requires Qaḍā’.

f: If a person becomes insane or faints for the entire duration of the month of Ramadan, must they make up the days?
b: No, Qaḍā’ is not required for the days of insanity or unconsciousness.

f: What is the obligation (Imsāk) for a person whose fast has been invalidated during the day?
b: They must refrain from eating or drinking for the remainder of the day.

f: Who is required to make up the day (Qaḍā’) after failing to fast due to the reasons listed in this chapter?
b: Those whose fast was invalidated, and women who were in a state of menstruation or post-partum bleeding at dawn.

f: What are the seven things considered disliked (Makrūh) for someone fasting?
b: 1. Tasting something (without excuse), 2. Chewing something (without excuse), 3. Chewing gum, 4. Kissing, 5. Physical intimacy (Mubāsharah), 6. Collecting and swallowing saliva, 7. Anything suspected of weakening the faster (e.g., bloodletting or cupping).

f: Is it disliked to apply oil to the mustache or kohl while fasting?
b: No, these are considered permissible.

f: What is the ruling on using the Miswāk while fasting?
b: It is permissible and remains Sunnah throughout the entire day, even at the end of the day, regardless of whether it is fresh or moistened with water.

f: Is it permissible to take a bath or wash oneself while fasting?
b: Yes.

f: What are the three recommended (Mustaḥabb) acts for one who is fasting?
b: Eating Suhur, delaying the Suhur (until just before dawn), and hastening the Iftār (breaking the fast).

f: Who is permitted to break their fast according to the chapter on impediments?
b: Those fearing increased illness, pregnant or nursing women fearing harm to themselves or their child, and those suffering from life-threatening hunger or thirst.

f: Is it better for a traveler to fast or break their fast?
b: Fasting is better if it does not harm them and companions are also fasting; otherwise, it is better to break the fast and join their companions.

f: What is the rule for making up missed fasts if someone dies before their excuse is removed?
b: They are not required to leave a will for fasting.

f: Must missed fasts (Qaḍā’) be performed on consecutive days?
b: No, consecutive days are not required.

f: If a new Ramadan approaches and one has missed fasts from a previous year, what is the priority?
b: Prioritize the new month of Ramadan; there is no penalty or expiation for delaying the makeup fast.

f: What is the Fidyah for an elderly or infirm person unable to fast?
b: Providing half a Ṣā‘ of wheat per day.

f: Can a voluntary faster break their fast without an excuse?
b: Yes.

f: Is hospitality considered a valid excuse to break a voluntary fast?
b: Yes, for both the guest and the host.

f: Must voluntary fasts that are spoiled be made up?
b: Yes, except for those started on the two Eids or Tashrīq days, which do not need to be made up (per Ẓāhir al-Riwāyah).

f: If someone vows to fast in Sha’bān, would fasting in Rajab satisfy it?
b: Yes, fasting in another month satisfies the vow.

f: Is fasting a requirement for all types of I‘tikāf?
b: No, fasting is only a condition for I‘tikāf that has been vowed.
